hypotheses.justification: The patch part never needs hX: `OutgoingDilation.correction_times_U_zero` only takes hXR. hX is used only through `heatE_times_U` → `heatE_before` → `HeatTailEdit.switch_zero`. Definitions: `heatE F XR p = OutgoingDilation.E F XR p * HeatTailEdit.multiplier h ν K p.1` with K = switchRadius F XR; `multiplier h ν K X = 1 + switch K X * (...)`; `switch K X = OutgoingSchedule.sigma (Real.log (X/K) / (3/10))`; `OutgoingDilation.U F XR p = F.U (p.1/XR, p.2)` with `Profile.U F p = F.logU (Real.log p.1, p.2)`. Since `Real.log_neg_eq_log` gives log(-x) = log x, for X ≤ 0 and Y = -X ≥ 0 we get switch K X = switch K Y and U F XR (X,eta) = U F XR (Y,eta). K > 0 by `switchRadius_pos` (uses hXR). Case Y ≤ K, which includes X = 0 because log 0 = 0: 0 ≤ Y/K ≤ 1, so `Real.log_nonpos` gives log(Y/K) ≤ 0, and `OutgoingSchedule.sigma_zero` (hypothesis x ≤ 0) gives switch = 0. Then the multiplier is 1 and heatE = OutgoingDilation.E at (X,eta). Case Y > K: `HeatedOutgoing.U_after_switch F XR eta Y hXR` gives U F XR (Y,eta) = 0, hence U F XR (X,eta) = 0, and both sides are 0. For X > 0 the existing proof applies. So the statement holds for all real X given hXR, and the proof just adds a case split on the sign of X.
